Alicia / team — I pulled together the technical artifact checklist you as auditors will care about and a couple implementation notes:

What Redwood can provide now:
- System configuration snapshots (monthly) and control owners for authentication/authorization.
- API call logs and processed event logs for the product surfaces you specified.
- KV cache hit/miss rates + trace IDs for sample requests (useful for forensics).
- Infrastructure change logs and IAM activity logs.

Retention carveout options:
- Option A (Audit slice): 365-day retention for named audit-log buckets (retains PII hashes, not raw payloads). No model output retention change.
- Option B (Full retention): 365-day retention including structured request metadata and expanded trace detail — requires a signed data handling addendum (we can draft).

Operational notes:
- Evidence handoff: we use a secure staging bucket for bulk artifact export. We'll provide a one-time export or an ongoing export cadence (weekly) depending on your preference.
- Cost: sustained 365d retention for Audit slice will add a storage surcharge; Marissa will include line items on the amendment.

Attachments: evidence-upload-guide.md (we already shared), SOC2-Summary-2026.pdf (controls map).

I'll also include a short checklist for your internal auditors to help prioritize which artifacts to request first (config snapshots, access lists, log indices).

—Ben Carter
